This catalogue lists every work that has come down to us under Plato's name: the thirty-six works that the scholar Thrasyllus arranged in nine groups of four (*tetralogies*) in the first century AD, the shorter works he set apart as spurious, and the short poems attributed to Plato.

Being transmitted under Plato's name is not the same as being written by him. Each entry therefore gives two separate pieces of information: where the work stands in the ancient collection, and how scholars judge its authorship today — **generally accepted**, **disputed**, or **generally considered not to be by Plato**. The thirteen *Letters* are assessed one by one. Where scholars disagree, we say so rather than choose a side.

The traditional division into early, middle and late dialogues is available only as an optional filter. It is a modern reconstruction based on style and content. The late group, identified through studies of Plato's style, rests on firmer ground than the others, and even there the order of the works is debated.

If you are new to Plato, start with the **reading selection**: twenty-five dialogues and the *Seventh Letter*, with fuller descriptions and suggestions on where to begin. Reading times and difficulty levels are rough editorial estimates. Links to external texts name the provider and the language; translations differ.
